Subject: Deployment mode follow-up - shared vs dedicated

Hi Samantha -

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed set of next steps so we stay aligned.

Recap (what we heard):
- FinPay is evaluating an LLM inference platform for transaction categorization and fraud signal enrichment.
- Primary concerns: predictable latency during peak windows, isolation from other tenants (noisy neighbor), and auditability for compliance.
- Procurement timeline: target decision by end of Q1 with a technical PO in Dec.

Deployment-mode summary:
- Hosted API: fastest to integrate (no infra footprint), but is multi-tenant. We offer per-tenant rate limits and caching; good for early integration and smaller workloads.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and stronger isolation (resource partitioning + isolated KV caches). Good middle ground for production workloads where noisy-neighbor risk matters.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full network and infrastructure isolation, customer-managed network/KMS. Recommended for regulated data environments or full audit isolation.

Noisy neighbor / isolation specifics (short):
- Dedicated capacity includes tenant-level resource reservations and placement policies to avoid co-tenancy on the same GPU host when requested.
- We run continuous telemetry on per-tenant p95/p99 latency and token throughput and have preemption and throttling policies to protect SLOs.
- For the highest isolation, Private VPC eliminates shared control plane networking and gives you customer-controlled ingress/egress.

Proposed next steps:
1) Schedule a 60-min infra deep-dive with your infra/security lead + our infra eng (Marissa) to go over isolation guarantees and monitoring (I can book for next week).
2) Share a short doc with our recommended configuration (attached: redwood-dedicated-architecture.pdf).
3) Follow-up on procurement: I'll attach an indicative pricing sheet and a draft SOW after the deep-dive.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-architecture.pdf (high level diagram + isolation controls)

If that plan looks good, I'll propose three times for a technical call.

Thanks -
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi Samantha -

Great questions - answers below and additional detail for the call.

1) Dedicated isolation guarantees:
- Dedicated = reserved capacity in a customer-specific pool. In our standard Dedicated product we provision isolated GPU instances within a customer pool (no cross-tenant scheduling on those instances). That means noisy-neighbor interference at the host level is very unlikely.
- We also offer a "single-tenant host" add-on (recommended if you need absolute host isolation) where your workloads are the only tenant on the physical host.

2) SLOs (typical):
- Hosted API: best-effort latency; p95 typically 150-500ms depending on model and seq length; p99 not SLA-backed.
- Dedicated (standard): SLA-backed throughput and a p95 target (e.g., 200-600ms) and p99 monitoring with alerting; we can negotiate p99 SLA for latency if you commit to a reserved capacity tier. For your requirement of p99 < 1s on enrichment, Dedicated is the safest fit; we can include an SLA clause in the SOW.

3) Private VPC:
- Typical deployment time 4-8 weeks for an initial VPC stack (shorter if your infra team provides direct access/VPN keys quickly).
- You get customer-managed networking, KMS integration, and full audit logs from the control plane. We can surface kernel-level telemetry if you require it - it's part of the Enterprise observability add-on and can be pushed to your monitoring endpoint (e.g., Datadog, Splunk).

Noisy-neighbor mitigations we use across Dedicated:
- Placement policies to avoid co-locating high-IO tenants
- Per-tenant KV cache and pre-warming for hot prefixes
- Rate-limited ingress with graceful degradation and fallback model variants
- Continuous per-tenant telemetry and auto-throttle/guardrails when abnormal burst patterns are detected

Pricing / time-to-prod (indicative):
- Dedicated: baseline reserved pool + per-token execution; typical time-to-prod 2-3 weeks after PO (depends on model onboarding).
- Private VPC: baseline infra + integration effort; 4-8 weeks.

I've attached an indicative pricing sheet and a draft SOW for procurement review (redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx, draft-sow-finpay.docx).

- If good, we'll bring Marissa (in infra) and Neha (security) to cover isolation and auditability.

Cheers,
